name: FL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Patronis's massive financial advantage ($3.8M raised vs $174K)
model.rationale: The R+18 district lean, Patronis's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending edge, and markets pricing him near 95% all point to a safe Republican hold. Valimont's modest war chest gives little reason to move off that picture.
model.watch: Any late independent polling showing Valimont within single digits, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign of a real contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jimmy Patronis, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to hold this Florida Panhandle seat, one of the most Republican districts in the state with an R+18 partisan lean. He has raised about $3.8 million and holds over $930,000 in cash, supported by roughly $2.1 million in outside spending, while Democrat Gay Valimont has raised about $174,000 with minimal outside help. Prediction markets give Patronis roughly a 95% chance of winning.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. An independent candidate is on the ballot but is not seen as a factor. The race is rated Safe Republican.
